subtype: Approach: track spending for a month, then set category limits [Revision]
passage:
Lakshmi: You look stressed. Short again this month?

Jyoti: Third month running. I don't get it. My salary isn't small.

Lakshmi: Do you know where it goes?

Jyoti: Not exactly. So I'm going to write down every payment I make from my phone, for one month. Everything.

(A month later, at the pantry.)

Jyoti: Look at this. Food delivery is the biggest item. More than transport and phone put together.

Lakshmi: Seriously? I would have guessed rent.

Jyoti: Rent is fixed. This is the leak. So now there's a weekly cap on delivery, and cooking twice.

Lakshmi: Easier than a guessed budget.

Jyoti: Yes. Numbers I can see are better than promises I make to myself.

qa.q: Which item was the biggest in Jyoti's month of records?
qa.a: Food delivery was the biggest item, more than transport and phone put together.

qa.q: What was Jyoti feeling when saying that the salary is not small?
qa.a: Jyoti felt puzzled and stressed at being short for the third month in a row.

qa.q: What could Jyoti try if the weekly cap keeps being broken, and why?
qa.a: Jyoti could cook more meals in advance so the cap is easy to keep, since the cap works only when an alternative exists.

qa.q: How might Lakshmi see the results compared with the earlier guess about rent?
qa.a: Lakshmi was surprised, because rent had been the guess, which shows how easily a guessed budget can miss the real leak.

grounding: After running short an employee records every payment for a month, finds the biggest leak and sets a weekly cap on it.
